To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rap2V12 transgenic mice displayed fewer and thinner dendritic spines, enhanced LTD, impaired spatial learning, and defective extinction of contextually cued fear.
Rap2 opposes ERK signaling in the hippocampus and in the amygdala, and thereby regulates dendritic spine formation, synaptic plasticity, and fear memory.
Rap2 signaling is required for dendritic spine maintenance and normal spatial learning and fear extinction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of synaptic plasticity and memory formation in the brain.
the role of Rap2 signaling in the brain and behavior.
the role of the Rap2 GTPase in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Rap2 protein is a negative regulator for synaptic plasticity and learning and memory.
the Rap signaling is important in learning, memory and synaptic plasticity, which are important in the development of the brain.
the Rap2 signaling in brain is important for synaptic plasticity, learning, and memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rap2 is an important regulator of synaptic plasticity and memory.

Rap2 is an important negative regulator of Ras–ERK in the brain, and that the balance of Ras–ER K and Rap2 signaling is important for the formation and maintenance of dendritic spines and for synaptic plasticity and memory.
Rap2V12 and Rap2N17 transgenic mice were created to study the role of Rap2 in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rap2 is a key negative regulator of Ras signaling in the brain.
the Rap2 signaling pathway is critical for normal synaptic and behavioral plasticity.
the Ras and Rap signaling pathways play opposing roles in synaptic plasticity and learning.
